title: Microsoft Entra ID: extended 30-day backup and recovery through Microsoft 365 Backup
summary: Hold: the recovery control pairs starting a restore with a history page that only reviews or cancels jobs, and the hybrid recovery guidance drops the documented group-membership exception. Most existing-feature details and roadmap facts are supported, but existing restore limits must not be promised for the undocumented extension.

claims.claim: Soft-delete recovery addresses deleted objects, whereas backup recovery can also roll back unintended attribute changes.
claims.quote:
Soft delete | Object is retained in a deleted state for a limited time
When combined with soft deletion, Microsoft Entra Backup and Recovery enables organizations to recover from unintended or malicious attribute changes and deletions.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/backup/soft-deletion to sources to support the explicit distinction between soft-delete recovery and recovery of modified objects.

claims.claim: The same existing restore behaviours and limits will apply to whatever Microsoft ships for the 30-day extension.
claims.quote: Searched: Entra 30-day Backup Storage enable default license roles objects residency; Entra 30-day backup Graph switch enable. Opened Entra overview, supported objects, recovery model and Graph backup overview; no text carries existing limits into the extension.
claims.fix: Replace the final sentence with 'Rehearse the existing recovery to build operational experience, but revalidate restore behaviour, limits and roles against the extension documentation when Microsoft publishes it.' Do not promise that existing recovery limits apply to an undocumented capability.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The governance checklist excludes all changes to synced users and groups even though the risk section retains the group-membership exception.
claims.quote: Risk: 'changes to on-premises synced objects (except group memberships) are excluded from recovery'. Guidance: 'List the users and groups synchronised from Active Directory Domain Services ... because their changes are excluded from recovery.'
claims.fix: In Before rollout, say 'Plan a separate backup for objects managed in AD DS; changes to synced objects, except group memberships, are excluded from Entra recovery.' Retain the exception from https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/backup/scope-supported-objects-limitations. Note that the recovery-model article gives a broader exclusion if discussing the documentation discrepancy.

claims.where: Governance controls: first paragraph after table
claims.claim: All rows after the extension row govern existing seven-day Entra recovery, including the Microsoft 365 Backup billing row.
claims.quote: 'The remaining rows govern the existing seven-day recovery' conflicts with 'General Microsoft 365 Backup control; not confirmed for the Entra extension' and 'Microsoft has not said that this meter applies to Entra objects'.
claims.fix: Replace 'The remaining rows govern the existing seven-day recovery' with 'The two Entra rows govern existing seven-day recovery. The billing row is general Microsoft 365 Backup context and is not documented as a control for existing Entra recovery or the planned extension.'

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist tells administrators to assign backup roles and require reviewed difference reports, but the controls table has no rows for those controls.
claims.quote: 'assign Microsoft Entra Backup Reader to reviewers and Microsoft Entra Backup Administrator' and 'require a reviewed difference report first'; table rows cover the extension switch, viewing backups, recovery jobs and billing only.
claims.fix: Add controls rows named 'Assigning Entra backup and recovery roles' and 'Creating and reviewing difference reports'. The existing view-backups and recovery-history rows do not describe either action; supply separately verified paths and API equivalents or explain the undocumented surface.
